Two cylindrical rods are bound with a strap. Each rod has diameter 12 cm . How long is the strap?
![](./images/841b8744-c0fe-4939-bfaf-937e2be63b06-242_268_516_2167_760.jpg)
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Each rod has radius 6 cm. For two equal touching rods, the strap contains two straight portions, each one diameter (12 cm), and two semicircles that together make one full circumference of radius 6 cm. Length = 24 + 2pi(6) = 24 + 12pi cm, approximately 61.7 cm.

stem:
A factory produces arc shaped tiles of different colors each of inner radius 7 inches. Arc length of each tile is 2 inches. Hamza wants to purchase these tiles for making a circular
![](./images/841b8744-c0fe-4939-bfaf-937e2be63b06-235_193_482_1246_1475.jpg)
design on the wall. How many tiles are required?
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: The required circumference has radius 7 inches, so its length is 2pi r = 14pi inches. Each tile covers 2 inches of arc, so the number is 14pi/2 = 7pi, approximately 21.99. Therefore 22 tiles are required.

stem: Draw an arc of any length. Complete the circle without finding its centre of which the given arc is the part.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Choose A, B and C on the arc. Build successive congruent triangles outward using the previous side lengths as described in the construction, producing D, E, F, G and H. Join the successive points with equal arcs until the original arc is completed into a circle; this construction does not locate the centre.
sectionLabel: (b) To Complete a Circle without Finding its Centre when Part of Circumference is Given

stem: Three non-collinear points $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and C are such that $\mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{BC}=3 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $\angle \mathrm{B}=120^{\circ}$. Construct a circle passing through $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and C .
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Construct AB = 3 cm. At B construct angle ABC = 120 degrees and mark C so BC = 3 cm. Draw perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC; they meet at O. Draw the circle centred at O through A (it also passes through B and C).
sectionLabel: To Draw a Circle Passing Through Three Non-Collinear Points

stem: PQ and QR are perpendicular segments in a plane such that $\mathrm{PQ}=4 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $\mathrm{QR}=3 \mathrm{~cm}$. Construct a circle passing through $\mathrm{P}, \mathrm{Q}$ and R . What is the radius of that circle?
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Draw PQ = 4 cm. At Q erect QR perpendicular to PQ and mark QR = 3 cm. Since triangle PQR is right-angled at Q, PR is its hypotenuse and the circle's diameter. PR = sqrt(4^2+3^2) = 5 cm, so the midpoint of PR is the centre and the radius is 2.5 cm.
sectionLabel: To Draw a Circle Passing Through Three Non-Collinear Points

stem: Given a circle, locate its centre.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Choose three points A, B and C on the circle and join them. Construct the perpendicular bisectors of two chords, such as AB and BC. Their intersection O is the centre of the circle.
sectionLabel: To Locate the Centre of a Circle

stem: Draw an arc and divide it into two equal parts.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Mark the endpoints A and B of the arc. Construct the perpendicular bisector of chord AB; it meets the arc at its midpoint M. Thus arcs AM and MB are equal.
sectionLabel: To Locate the Centre of a Circle

stem: Three points $\mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}$ and Z are located on an arc. Find the centre of that arc.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Join X, Y and Z to form two chords, for example XY and YZ. Construct the perpendicular bisectors of both chords. Their intersection O is the centre of the arc's circle.
sectionLabel: To Locate the Centre of a Circle

stem: Draw a circle with the help of any round object, then find its centre.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Trace the round object. Mark any three points A, B and C on the circle and join two chords. Construct the perpendicular bisectors of the chords; their intersection is the centre.
sectionLabel: To Locate the Centre of a Circle

stem: Find the centre of an arc DEF , such that chord $\mathrm{DE}=3.5 \mathrm{~cm}$, chord $\mathrm{EF}=4.2 \mathrm{~cm}$ and angle between both segments is $60^{\circ}$.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Construct angle DEF = 60 degrees. On its arms mark DE = 3.5 cm and EF = 4.2 cm, then join D to F. Construct perpendicular bisectors of DE and EF. Their intersection O is equidistant from D, E and F, so O is the centre of the required arc.
sectionLabel: To Locate the Centre of a Circle

stem: Construct a circle of radius 3 cm . Draw two tangents from a point $\mathrm{A}, 5.8 \mathrm{~cm}$ away from the centre of circle.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Draw the circle with centre O and radius 3 cm, then mark A with OA = 5.8 cm. Bisect OA at Q and draw the auxiliary circle centred at Q with radius QO. It cuts the given circle at T1 and T2. Join AT1 and AT2; these are the required tangents.

stem:
A circular mirror with radius 20 cm hangs by a wire from a hook. The wire is 30 cm long and is a tangent to the mirror in two places. How far above the top of the mirror is the hook?
![](./images/841b8744-c0fe-4939-bfaf-937e2be63b06-243_465_386_345_878.jpg)
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: The 30 cm wire forms two equal tangent segments, so each is 15 cm. A radius to a tangent point is perpendicular to the wire. If O is the mirror centre and H the hook, OH = sqrt(20^2 + 15^2) = 25 cm. The top of the mirror is 20 cm above O, so the hook is 25 - 20 = 5 cm above the top.
sectionLabel: Tangent to the Circle

stem: Draw an arc of any length. Draw a tangent without using centre, through point $A$, when point A is: (i) in the middle of arc. (ii) at the right end of the arc.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: (i) If A is the midpoint of arc AP, join the arc endpoints, construct the perpendicular bisector through A, then draw through A a line parallel to the chord; it is the tangent. (ii) If A is an endpoint, join it to another point on the arc, use the chord's perpendicular bisector to locate an auxiliary point on the arc, copy the prescribed equal lengths at A, and draw the resulting ray through A as the tangent.
sectionLabel: Tangent to the Circle

stem: Draw an arc ABC . Take a point X outside the arc and draw a tangent from X to the arc without using centre of the arc.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Draw line XB to meet the arc again at C. Bisect XB at M and draw the semicircle with centre M and radius MX. At C erect a perpendicular to XB meeting the semicircle at D. With centre X and radius XD, cut the given arc at E. Join XE; XE is the required tangent.
sectionLabel: Tangent to the Circle

stem: Construct a circle of radius 4 cm . Mark a point P on the circumference and draw a tangent passing through P .
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Draw the circle with centre O and radius 4 cm. Mark P on it and join OP. At P construct a line perpendicular to OP. This line is the tangent through P.
sectionLabel: Tangent to the Circle

stem: Construct two intersecting circles of radii 2.5 cm and 3 cm whose centres are 4.8 cm apart. Draw two common tangents to the circles.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Draw centres A and B with AB = 4.8 cm. Draw circles of radii 2.5 cm and 3 cm; they intersect. Bisect AB at M and draw the semicircle on AB. Extend the common chord to meet this semicircle, use the resulting auxiliary point to locate equal tangent points on the circles, and join those points. Repeat symmetrically for the second common tangent.
sectionLabel: To draw a Tangent to two Unequal Intersecting Circles

stem:
Construct two touching circles of radii 2.6 cm and 3.6 cm . Draw:
(i) a common tangent that passes through the point of contact of both circles.
(ii) a common tangent that does not pass through the point of contact of both circles.
(iii) two common tangents.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Construct the two circles with centres 6.2 cm apart so they touch externally. The common tangent through their contact point is perpendicular to the line of centres. Construct the two remaining direct common tangents using the auxiliary-circle method based on the radius difference, 3.6 - 2.6 = 1 cm. These give the requested tangent through contact and the two tangents not through contact.
sectionLabel: To draw a Tangent to two Unequal Touching Circles

stem:
Encircle the correct option in the following.
i. Angle between tangent and radial segment of a circle is:

(b) non-collinear

(d) coincident
vi. In which type of triangle, incentre and circumcenter are coincident?
(a) scalene
(b) isosceles
(c) equilateral
(d) right triangle

(a) 4 cm
(b) 8 cm
(c) 8.8 cm
(d) 0.8 cm
viii. Two tangents are drawn at the ends of diameter of a circle of radius 3.5 cm .
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: i. (d) 90 degrees; ii. (a) parallel; iii. (b) 2; iv. (c) 6.2 cm; v. (a) collinear; vi. (c) equilateral; vii. (d) 0.8 cm; viii. (b) 7 cm; ix. (a) 1 point; x. (d) 3 cm; xi. (c) 10 cm; xii. (d) chords; xiii. (b) 1; xiv. (d) infinitely many pairs.
sectionLabel: To draw Direct Common Tangents (External Tangents) to two Equal Circles

stem:
Construct two equal circles each of radius 3 cm . Centres of the circles are 6 cm apart. Draw their:
(i) direct common tangents.
(ii) transverse common tangents.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Draw AB = 6 cm and circles of radius 3 cm at A and B; they touch externally. For direct tangents, draw equal perpendicular radii at A and B and join corresponding endpoints, giving two parallel tangents. The transverse tangents coincide at the circles' common contact point in this limiting touching case, so there are not two distinct transverse common tangents.
sectionLabel: To draw Direct Common Tangents (External Tangents) to two Equal Circles

stem:
Construct two circles of radii 2 cm and 3.5 cm . Draw:
(ii) direct common tangents
(ii) transvers common tangents to the circles, if the distances between centres of circles is 6.4 cm .
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Draw AB = 6.4 cm and circles centred at A and B with radii 3.5 cm and 2 cm. For direct tangents use an auxiliary circle at A of radius 1.5 cm (difference of radii), construct tangents from B to it, then draw parallels at distance 2 cm to obtain the two external tangents. For transverse tangents use an auxiliary circle at A of radius 5.5 cm (sum of radii), construct tangents from B, and transfer them to the original circles to obtain the two internal tangents.
sectionLabel: To draw Direct Common Tangents to two Unequal Circles

stem:
Construct a circle of radius 2.5 cm . Draw two tangents making an angle of:
(i) $45^{\circ}$
(ii) $90^{\circ}$ with each other.
keyPoints: ["Use the chapter's stated circle-construction and tangent properties; preserve all given measurements."]
modelAnswer: Draw the circle with centre O and radius 2.5 cm. For tangents meeting at angle theta, choose two radii whose angle at O is 180 degrees - theta, and draw perpendiculars to the radii at their endpoints. Thus use central angles 135 degrees for theta = 45 degrees and 90 degrees for theta = 90 degrees; each pair of perpendiculars meets at the required angle.
sectionLabel: To Draw two Tangents to a Circle Meeting each other at a Given Angle
